strongest_angle: Analyzing the intersection of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's rational detective Sherlock Holmes and H.P. Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos reveals chronological discrepancies and thematic clashes between 1880-1914 settings and 1925-1935 mythos tales.

key_facts.fact: Neil Gaiman wrote the short story A Study in Emerald as a Sherlock Holmes pastiche transferred to the Cthulhu Mythos universe, which won the 2004 Hugo Award for Best Short Story.
James Lovegrove noted that original Sherlock Holmes stories take place roughly between 1880 and 1914, whereas Cthulhu Mythos tales are mostly contemporary to 1925 and 1935.
Sherlock Holmes vs. Cthulhu is set in England in 1890, where human remains and strange spherical bones incised with unusual designs have been found in London's East End.

quotes.text: My aim with the trilogy is to tie the two fictional worlds as tightly and tidily together as I can.
quotes.speaker: James Lovegrove

quotes.text: Sherlock Holmes vs. Cthulhu is set in England in 1890. Human remains have been found in London’s East End: bones, piled up in strange ways, along with strange spherical bones incised with unusual designs.
quotes.speaker: Kam Martinez
